subject: Clarifying Limited Audit Mechanism & Evidence Sprint (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@clearspringhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@clearspringhealth.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.g@ctsec.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA - security exhibit questions

Thanks, Rachel — we reviewed your MSA redlines and the security exhibit. A few open items from Clearspring's side that will block sign: 1) SOC 2 evidence cadence / attestation delivery (we typically expect Type II on file for the prior 12 months), 2) penetration test notice window and scope (we prefer a 21-day notice and an option for joint- scoping), and 3) the breadth of "audit rights" language — legal wants a narrower operational view rather than broad inspection rights.

Can you share a short SOC2 summary (what assertions are in scope) and an example of how Redwood intends to schedule evidence/review so our security team can map to internal audit processes? Also attaching a sample list of evidence items we would ask for so we can compare notes.

--
Daniel Lee
Head of Security Programs
Clearspring Health
Attachment stubs: Clearspring_evidence_sample.xlsx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA - security exhibit questions

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Quick replies and a proposed path forward: 

1) SOC 2: we can provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report within our redline (we typically share a redacted version on execution and full report under an NDA); attaching a 1-page SOC2 summary that lists the applicable Trust Services Criteria and sample controls.

2) Pen test: Redwood's standard is a 30-day notice for customer-conducted or customer-requested pen tests when non-prod access is required; we can negotiate to 21 days for joint-scoped engagements. We prefer to keep emergency/incident-driven tests separate. 

3) Audit rights scope: propose a limited mechanism in the MSA + explicit Order Form appendix: - bounded inspections (max 4/year), - evidence sprint model (timeboxed week to pull evidence), - non-production staging access for live demonstrations where needed, - sample-set based requests (top 5 components), - technical guardrails (no privileged creds, masked PII, read-only access).

Action: I've attached our redlines to the MSA and the SOC2 summary. Can your team review the proposed limited-inspection paragraph in the attached PDF and confirm whether 21 days for pen tests is a hard requirement? If so, we can update to 21 days and adjust the Order Form appendix. If not, we'd ask for written justification for <21 to route through legal.

Next step: looping in Karthik and Priyom on legal language; Marissa to coordinate operational runbook if we land on the appendix approach.

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redlines_MSA_clearspring_20270110.pdf; SOC2_Summary_Clearspring_20270109.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@clearspringhealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@clearspringhealth.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA - security exhibit questions

On Jan 10, Rachel wrote with a good compromise. Draft suggested language below (excerpt for discussion) — I'd prefer to keep the high-level right to evidence but tightly scoped in the exhibit: 

"Limited Inspection Mechanism. Customer may request operational evidence and limited inspection of Redwood's controls as set forth in this Security Exhibit. Inspection requests shall be timeboxed to an Evidence Sprint (no longer than five business days from kickoff), limited to a sample set of components listed in the Order Form appendix, and may occur no more than four (4) times per rolling twelve (12) month period. Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted as appropriate) within seven (7) business days of execution of the Order Form and thereafter upon renewal. Penetration testing by or on behalf of Customer requires no less than thirty (30) calendar days' prior notice; parties may agree to a twenty-one (21) day notice for jointly-scoped engagements with mutually agreed test boundaries. Access to live systems will be provisioned in non-production staging environments where possible; production-level access will be escalated and provisioned only with documented scope, read-only credentials, and data-masking requirements."
I attached our internal pen test template (pen_test_template_ri.docx) and a redline snippet that replaces broad "audit rights" language with the above structure. Key legal considerations: avoid open-ended "inspection" wording that would permit unbounded forensic access; require ticketing & pre-approved scope; indemnity/insurance carveouts are out of scope for this clause.

--
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pen_test_template_ri.docx

From: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@clearspringhealth.com>
To: Priya Menon <priya.m@clearspringhealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.g@ctsec.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA - security exhibit questions

Thanks, Priyom and team — the suggested language narrows things in the right places and the Evidence Sprint concept is workable. A couple of asks from Clearspring: 

- Pen test notice: Cleanspring's policy baseline is 21 days for scheduling and internal approvers; would Redwood accept 21 days for customer-initiated tests?
- Evidence cadence: we would like one of the four inspections to be a joint tabletop or walkthrough (live call + brief demo) rather than purely document-based; please confirm staging access is feasible for that.
- SLA / escalation: if Redwood misses an agreed evidence sprint deadline (e.g., fails to provide requested artifacts within the five business day window), we'd like a remediation plan and the option to request a follow-up limited inspection without counting against the annual caps.

If you can accommodate 21 days for pen tests and commit to the remediation path, Clearspring will accept the Order Form appendix approach and we can proceed to sign.

Regards,
Daniel
Head of Security Programs
Clearspring Health

Subject: Re: Draft MSA - security exhibit questions

Follow-up from ops side — happy to coordinate the Evidence Sprint logistics if legal lands on the language. Proposed runbook and timeline: 

1) Pre-kickoff (wd0): agree sample-set in Order Form appendix and identify primary contacts (Clearspring: Daniel/Alicia; Redwood: Marissa + eng oncall).
2) Kickoff (wd1): 30-minute sync to align scope and confirm artifacts list; open evidence ticket in our secure intake board (link in ticket).
3) Evidence pull (wd2-wd4): Redwood provides documents, screenshots, and redacted logs; for staging demos, schedule a 60-minute walkthrough.
4) Close (wd5): final confirmation and short summary memo; if any artifact gaps, Redwood will publish a remediation plan within three business days and propose a date for a follow-up limited inspection (does not count against the cap if remediation impacted by Redwood).

I will create an Evidence Sprint template and a pre-approved artifact checklist and share via Drive. Alicia — if you can confirm internal approvers for the tabletop/demonstration, I'll invite them to the ticket and block a placeholder week for Q1 (week of 2027-02-14).

Next steps: legal to confirm final wording for the MSA exhibit and Order Form appendix; ops will draft the intake ticket and checklist once language is signed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Assurance Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: Evidence_Sprint_Template.xlsx
